title: Hawaii: history overview
d: Hawaii: the Aloha State, admitted 1959 (50th); capital Honolulu.
definition: Hawaii: the Aloha State, admitted 1959 (50th); capital Honolulu.
description: Hawaii — "Aloha State" — entered the Union 1959 (50th). Its capital is Honolulu and its largest city is Honolulu. Polynesian voyagers c. 1000 AD. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Hawaii achieved statehood 1959 (50th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Kingdom; overthrow 1893. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Hawaii its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Hawaii went from territory to state.
definition: How Hawaii went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Hawaii: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Pearl Harbor 1941; statehood 1959. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Hawaii's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Honolulu
d: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii.
definition: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii.
description: Honolulu has been the seat of Hawaii government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Hawaii's largest is Honolulu — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Aloha State
description: The nickname "Aloha State" captures how Hawaii sees itself — and how America sees it. Statehood in 1959 made it the 50th state. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Ua mau ke ea o ka aina i ka pono (The life of the land is perpetuated in righteousness)."

definition: The state motto of Hawaii is "Ua mau ke ea o ka aina i ka pono (The life of the land is perpetuated in righteousness)."
description: The motto "Ua mau ke ea o ka aina i ka pono (The life of the land is perpetuated in righteousness)" is Hawaii's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Union Jack canton with eight stripes. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
